Speaker Script (0:00 - 0:45): Good morning respected committee members, evaluators, and supervisors. My name is Shahzaib Hussain, and I am presenting our Final Year Project entitled 'Emotion-Aware Interaction Using Facial Expression and Sentiment Analysis', conducted under the joint supervision of Dr. Ijaz Hussain from PIEAS and Dr. Noman Mazhar from ICCC. This project focuses on building a real-time multimodal perception architecture enabling machines to perceive human affective cues across visual, vocal, and textual modalities for empathetic interaction.
1. Introduction & Context
Background & Motivation: Why Emotion-Aware Interaction?
Slide 02 / 12
🔍 The Emotional Blindness in AI
  • Affective Computing Foundation: Human communication is overwhelmingly nonverbal. Albert Mehrabian’s 7-38-55 rule establishes that only 7% of emotional meaning is in spoken words, while 38% is vocal prosody and 55% is facial expression.
  • Industry 5.0 Human-Centric Shift: Modern assistive and service robotics must advance beyond repetitive automation to achieve empathetic collaboration, trust building, and cognitive alignment.
  • Unimodal Fragility: Standalone vision fails under poor lighting or head turns; standalone speech fails under ambient noise. Joint multimodal perception resolves ambiguity.
Key Insight: True empathy requires perceiving the synchronization between what a person looks like, how they say it, and what words they choose.
👥 Real-World Relevance & Beneficiaries
  • Assistive Healthcare & Eldercare: Social robots (e.g. NAO, Pepper) monitoring emotional well-being, detecting depression, anxiety, or acute distress in eldercare and clinical therapy.
  • Affective Education & Tutoring: Intelligent tutoring robots dynamically adjusting lesson difficulty and pedagogy when detecting student frustration or confusion.
  • Human-Robot Collaboration (HRC): Detecting cognitive overload and operator stress on industrial assembly lines to ensure occupational safety.
  • Conversational Agents: Empathetic virtual assistants adapting conversational tone in customer service and mental health crisis hotlines.
Speaker Script (0:45 - 1:35): Traditional AI systems process words but remain emotionally blind. Psychological studies prove that over 90% of affective cues are transmitted nonverbally. In healthcare, eldercare, and education, an emotionally unresponsive robot can cause alienation. Our motivation is to equip interactive systems with multimodal perception—combining vision, speech acoustics, and text sentiment—so intelligent agents can adapt their behavior contextually and empathetically.
2. Problem Definition
Problem Statement: The In-The-Wild Generalization Breakdown
Slide 03 / 12
⚠️ The Core Problem: Lab-to-Real-World Degradation

Current affective computing systems demonstrate remarkable performance in controlled laboratory environments (>90% accuracy), but catastrophically collapse when deployed in real-world interactive settings.

  • Visual Vulnerabilities: Lighting shifts, shadows, head-pose rotations, and camera motion blur destroy facial landmark detection.
  • Acoustic Corruptions: Ambient noise, room reverberation (RIR), microphone distance, and robot cooling fan ego-noise corrupt speech features.
  • Empirical Degradation Gap (Parihar et al., 2026 Survey across 42 studies):
    • Facial Emotion Recognition (FER) drops by 14.4% ± 7.1% in real-world deployments.
    • Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) drops by 8.6% ± 3.0% in operational environments.
Empirical Fact: Unimodal systems deployed on physical robots experience up to a 27.5% drop in accuracy when unconstrained users interact freely.
🔬 Data & Deployment Bottlenecks
  • Single-Corpus Overfitting: Models trained on single datasets (e.g. RAVDESS alone) memorize actor vocal tract quirks and sentence structures, collapsing below 50% accuracy on new speakers.
  • Severe Class Imbalance: Benchmark datasets exhibit extreme skew. For example, in FER2013, Disgust comprises only 1.55% of samples compared to 24.7% for Happy. Naive models completely ignore minority distress signals.
  • The Latency Penalty: Heavy multimodal cloud LLM pipelines require multi-second round trips, violating the sub-100ms conversational budget required for human rapport.
Our Target Solution: A cross-corpus trained, imbalance-resilient, sub-20ms edge-deployable multimodal architecture.
Speaker Script (1:35 - 2:25): The core problem we solve is the 'In-The-Wild Generalization Breakdown'. As documented in a 2026 Discover Robotics survey synthesizing 42 empirical studies, facial emotion models suffer a 14.4% average drop in accuracy when deployed on physical robots due to lighting and head pose shifts. Similarly, speech models degrade by 8.6% due to ambient and motor noise. Classifiers trained on a single recording studio overfit to individual actor vocal tracts, dropping cross-corpus accuracy. Finally, acute class imbalance causes standard models to ignore critical minority emotions like disgust.
3. Goals & Boundaries
Aim, Specific Objectives, Requirements & Scope
Slide 04 / 12
🎯 Project Aim & 4 Key Objectives
Core Aim: To design, develop, and benchmark an end-to-end, real-time emotion-aware multimodal interaction system that robustly detects human affect from facial expressions and vocal acoustics, dynamically synthesizing decisions for empathetic human-machine collaboration.
  • Objective 1 (FER): Engineer a multi-backbone neural ensemble (CNN + ViT) under class-balanced focal loss to achieve >70% accuracy across severe class skews.
  • Objective 2 (SER): Construct a 2,107-dimensional cross-corpus speech pipeline integrating handcrafted acoustic biomarkers and GPU Wav2Vec2 SSL across 12,162 recordings.
  • Objective 3 (Fusion): Develop a Dirichlet-optimized soft-voting engine to dynamically weight multimodal confidence distributions.
  • Objective 4 (Deployment): Package the entire perception stack into a standalone, edge-deployable bundle achieving sub-50ms latency (RTF << 1.0).
📋 Requirements & Project Boundaries
  • Functional Requirements:
    • Live video capture with real-time face detection & 7-class affect probabilities.
    • 16 kHz audio capture with energy VAD trimming & 6-class voice affect probabilities.
    • Unified posterior probability fusion & prosodic diagnostic extraction.
  • Non-Functional Requirements:
    • Real-time execution: perception latency < 50 ms.
    • Strict zero statistical data leakage across folds.
  • Project Boundaries (What is NOT Included):
    • Invasive physiological hardware (no EEG caps or GSR finger sensors).
    • Mechanical chassis manufacturing (focus is on AI perception intelligence).
Speaker Script (2:25 - 3:15): Our project aim is to build a reliable, real-time multimodal affective perception architecture. We set four specific engineering objectives: First, develop a facial model combining local convolutions and global attention that handles severe class imbalance. Second, build a cross-corpus speech emotion recognition system integrating over 12,000 voice recordings across four corpora. Third, develop a Dirichlet-optimized soft-voting fusion engine. And fourth, package the entire system for real-time edge execution with sub-50ms latency.
4. Literature Review (Part 1)
Literature Review: Unimodal vs. Multimodal Landscape in HRI
Slide 05 / 12
👁️ Facial Emotion Systems
  • Ruiz-García et al. (2018): Deployed CNN-LSTM on NAO robot. Lab accuracy reached 96.3%, but plummeted to 68.8% in real-world tests due to head-pose shifts.
  • Chiurco et al. (2021) & Valagkouti et al. (2022): Benchmarked DeepFace on NAO/Pepper. Found severe failures on Disgust (0% accuracy) and Surprise (40%).
  • Melinte & Vladareanu (2020): ResNet-50 / VGG-16 with Rectified Adam achieved 90.1% on CK+ benchmark.
🎙️ Speech Emotion Systems
  • Grágeda et al. (2023, 2024): Deployed distant SER on PR2 robot. Proved that room reverberation (RIR) and fan ego-noise severely corrupt acoustic features (+180% CCC improvement using LadderNet beamforming).
  • Lakomkin et al. (2018): Evaluated deep neural networks on iCub robot; proved necessity of noise data augmentation.
  • Chen et al. (2020): Fuzzy Random Forest on mobile robot reached 86.7% lab vs 79.1% real-world accuracy.
🔄 Multimodal Fusion Shift
  • Parihar et al. (2026 PRISMA Survey): Synthesized 42 studies (2015-2025). Multimodal systems grew to 53% of literature, providing +10% to +25% accuracy gain over unimodal systems.
  • Garcia, Gomez-Donoso & Cazorla (2024/2025): Multimodal Pepper assistant integrating 2D-CNN, 1D-CNN, and Mixtral LLM, demonstrating that multimodal fusion eliminates unimodal blind spots.
Literature Consensus: Multimodal integration is essential for robustness in ambient environments.
Speaker Script (3:15 - 4:05): In our literature review, we analyzed recent benchmark studies from 2015 to 2025. In facial analysis, studies on the NAO robot by Ruiz-García and Valagkouti proved that while CNNs perform well on happy expressions, they drop sharply in real-world deployment and fail on rare classes like disgust. In speech emotion recognition, research on the PR2 and iCub robots by Grágeda and Lakomkin showed that room reverberation and motor ego-noise severely corrupt acoustic features. The universal conclusion across the literature is that unimodal systems are insufficient. Over 53% of recent systems have adopted multimodal fusion because fusing audio and visual cues consistently delivers a 10% to 25% performance improvement under real-world noise.

🚀 Identified Research Gaps & Our Proposed Solutions
  • Gap 1: Single-Corpus Overfitting → Our Solution: Unified 4 distinct benchmark corpora (CREMA-D, RAVDESS, SAVEE, TESS) indexing 12,162 recordings across 121 speakers with strict speaker-independent partitioning.
  • Gap 2: Minority Class Neglect → Our Solution: Fused EfficientNet-B2, ResNet-50, and ViT-B/16 under Class-Balanced Focal Label Smoothing Loss, boosting Disgust F1 from 0% to 71.70%.
  • Gap 3: Cloud Latency Bottleneck → Our Solution: Serialized standalone production bundle running locally on RTX 5090 / CPU in ~16.1 ms (RTF = 0.0064 << 1.0).
Speaker Script (4:05 - 4:55): Slide 6 provides a direct comparison between our work and prior systems. Valagkouti's NAO system relied solely on DeepFace for a quiz game—it had zero speech capabilities and scored 0% on disgust. Garcia's Pepper assistant achieved high accuracy, but it required collecting a custom 5-minute training dataset for every new user and relied on heavy cloud GPUs. Our work addresses these exact gaps: First, we eliminate single-corpus overfitting by training across 4 speech corpora with 12,162 recordings. Second, our Class-Balanced Focal Loss achieves 71.7% F1 on minority disgust expressions. And third, rather than relying on cloud APIs, our system executes locally in ~16 milliseconds.
5. Methodology & System Design (Part 1)
Proposed Methodology: Dual-Branch Multimodal Architecture
Slide 07 / 12
⚙️ Perception Streams Breakdown
  • Visual Stream (FER):
    • Input: RGB 224x224 normalized face crops.
    • Multi-Backbone: EfficientNet-B2 (local edges) + ResNet-50 (deep residuals) + ViT-B/16 (global attention).
    • Optimization: Class-Balanced Focal Loss + RAdam.
  • Auditory Stream (SER):
    • Preprocessing: 16 kHz standardization, Energy VAD, Pre-emphasis (0.97), and Z-normalization.
    • 2,107 Total Features: 571 Handcrafted (Teager Energy TEO, F0 pitch, HNR, Jitter/Shimmer, 40 MFCCs, 64 Log-Mel) + 1,536 GPU Wav2Vec2 SSL (Layers 9 & 12).
    • Leakage-Free Selection: Imputer + IQR Scaling + Collinear pruning (|r| > 0.975).
    • Ensemble: Dirichlet Validation-Optimized Soft-Voting.
  • Agile Software Development Lifecycle:
    • Sprint 1: Facial Pipeline & Class-Balanced Focal Loss.
    • Sprint 2: Multi-Corpus Speech Indexing & Wav2Vec2 Extraction.
    • Sprint 3: Multimodal Fusion & Edge UI Dashboard.
Speaker Script (4:55 - 5:45): Slide 7 illustrates our end-to-end architecture and software development methodology. Our perception system operates on three parallel streams: In the visual branch, 224x224 face crops are processed by a multi-backbone ensemble combining EfficientNet-B2, ResNet-50, and Vision Transformer ViT-B/16, balancing fine local facial details with global attention. In the auditory branch, 16 kHz audio is processed through energy-based Voice Activity Detection to remove silence, followed by our dual-branch feature extractor: 571 handcrafted acoustic parameters capturing vocal tract tension and pitch, plus 1,536 deep self-supervised embeddings from GPU Wav2Vec2. All features pass through a leakage-free selector before being classified by a Dirichlet soft-voting ensemble. We implemented this architecture using an Agile Scrum workflow with bi-weekly iterative sprints.
5. Methodology & System Design (Part 2)
Software Engineering: Sequence Flow & Behavioral State Machine
Slide 08 / 12
🔄 System Interaction Sequence Flow
  • Step 1 (User Trigger): User initiates interaction or looks toward the camera.
  • Step 2 (Synchronous Capture): PyAudio buffers 16 kHz audio while OpenCV buffers video frames at 15 fps.
  • Step 3 (Parallel Perception Inference):
    • Video Frames → ViT-CNN Ensemble → P_visual(Emotion)
    • Audio Buffer → VAD → Handcrafted + Wav2Vec2 → P_vocal(Emotion)
    • Transcribed Text → Transformer Sentiment Head → Lexical Valence
  • Step 4 (Contextual Decision & Multimodal Fusion):
    • Blends probabilities: P_final(c) = w_v · P_visual + w_a · P_vocal + w_t · P_text
    • Dynamic Uncertainty Weighting: If face is occluded or lighting is poor, weight w_v shifts automatically to vocal prosody w_a.
  • Step 5 (Adaptive Action Execution): Generates empathetic spoken feedback via TTS and adapts interaction state.
🛡️ Behavioral State Machine & Fault Tolerance
  • State 1: IDLE / LISTENING: Continuously monitors ambient energy; triggers VAD when threshold exceeds 0.05 · max(E).
  • State 2: AFFECT EXTRACTION: Computes 2,107 acoustic dimensions & visual attention maps in parallel (~16 ms latency).
  • State 3: AMBIGUITY RESOLUTION: Resolves high-arousal overlap between Anger and Happy using pitch contour slope and lexical sentiment.
  • Robustness & Fault Tolerance:
    • Microphone Dropout: Automatic fallback to pure visual FER.
    • Camera Occlusion / Dark Room: Automatic fallback to pure audio SER.
    • Zero-Freeze Guarantee: Pre-cached bundle ensures no UI stalls.
Software Design Principle: Strict loose coupling between sensory ingestion daemons and the multimodal decision engine.
Speaker Script (5:45 - 6:35): Slide 8 displays our software engineering sequence flow and behavioral state machine. During an interaction, audio and video are buffered synchronously. The visual ensemble outputs posterior probabilities while the speech pipeline extracts acoustic and SSL embeddings. Crucially, our software architecture incorporates dynamic uncertainty weighting: If a user turns their head or lighting drops, the vision confidence drops, and the fusion engine automatically transfers decision weight to vocal prosody. Conversely, if high ambient noise corrupts the microphone, the system relies primarily on facial expressions. This mutual fallback ensures reliable, continuous operation without freezing or degrading the user experience.
6. Technology Stack
Technologies, Tools & Hardware Stack Justification
Slide 09 / 12
🧠 Deep Learning & Transformers (AI/ML)
  • PyTorch 2.11 & Torchvision / Torchaudio: Core neural backbone training & tensor operations.

✓ Justification: Allows heavy transformer passes locally with zero cloud API subscription costs.

  • Frontend: Jupyter Interactive Widgets (ipywidgets), HTML5 Audio API.

Speaker Script (6:35 - 7:15): Slide 9 outlines our technology stack and hardware setup. For deep learning, we utilize PyTorch 2.11 and Hugging Face transformers, taking advantage of Wav2Vec2 for speech representations and Vision Transformers for facial attention, alongside Scikit-Learn and XGBoost. Audio signal processing is implemented using Librosa and SciPy Signal for pitch and spectral feature extraction, while OpenCV handles facial bounding box tracking. On the hardware side, all models are accelerated on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 with 24GB VRAM, enabling transformer forward passes in under 8 milliseconds. Finally, the system is serialized into standalone Joblib and PyTorch bundles, with testing dashboards built using Jupyter widgets and HTML5 audio, fully version-controlled on GitHub.
7. Initial Progress (FER Milestone)
Preliminary Work: Facial Emotion Recognition Pipeline
Slide 10 / 12
📊 FER Methodology & Test Benchmark
  • Dataset Profiling (FER2013):
    • 35,887 total facial crops (28,709 train, 7,178 test).
    • Severe Skew: Disgust is only 1.55% of test data (111 samples) vs Happy at 24.71% (1,774 samples).
  • Multi-Backbone Dynamic Ensemble:
    • EfficientNet-B2 (9.1M) + ResNet-50 (25.6M) + ViT-B/16 (86.6M).
    • Class-Balanced Focal Label Smoothing Loss (γ=2.0, α=0.1) with inverse-frequency weighted sampling.
    • RAdam optimizer with Cosine Annealing Restarts.
  • Verified Empirical Achievements (7,178 Test Samples):
    • Overall Test Accuracy: 71.38% (vs ~65% standard baseline).
    • Macro F1: 70.24% | Weighted F1: 71.38%.
    • Minority Class Victory: 71.70% F1 on Disgust (68.47% recall, 75.25% precision) on merely 111 samples!
    • Top Classes: Happy (89.00% F1), Surprise (81.78% F1), Neutral (68.38% F1).
    • Best checkpoint exported at Epoch 8.
Speaker Script (7:15 - 8:05): Moving to our completed Semester 1 achievements: Slide 10 presents our Facial Emotion Recognition milestone. We evaluated on the challenging FER2013 benchmark of 35,887 images. The central difficulty was acute class imbalance: disgust accounts for merely 1.55% of the data. To overcome this, we built a multi-backbone dynamic ensemble combining EfficientNet-B2, ResNet-50, and Vision Transformer ViT-B/16, trained under Class-Balanced Focal Loss with inverse-frequency sampling. As shown in our normalized confusion matrix on the left, our model achieves a state-of-the-art 71.38% test accuracy and a 70.24% Macro F1. Crucially, rather than collapsing to zero on rare classes, our model attains 71.70% F1 on Disgust and 89.0% F1 on Happy. The best checkpoint was saved at Epoch 8 and exported for production.

Speaker Script (8:05 - 8:55): Slide 11 highlights our second completed milestone: the Speech Emotion Recognition pipeline. To eliminate single-corpus overfitting, we unified 12,162 recordings from CREMA-D, RAVDESS, SAVEE, and TESS across 121 speakers with strict speaker-independent partitioning. We extracted a massive 2,107-dimensional hybrid representation: 571 handcrafted acoustic parameters capturing vocal tract tension and pitch contours, combined with 1,536 deep self-supervised embeddings from GPU Wav2Vec2. As shown in our comparative benchmark graph on the left, our validation-optimized Dirichlet Soft-Voting Ensemble achieved 56.10% Validation Accuracy and 52.40% Test Accuracy on completely unseen actors, outperforming individual SVM, LightGBM, XGBoost, and MLP models. Most importantly, end-to-end inference executes in just 16.1 milliseconds—giving a Real-Time Factor of 0.0064, which is over 150 times faster than real-time playback.

🛡️ Risk Management & Mitigation Strategies
  • Risk 1: Real-World Acoustic Ego-Noise & Reverberation
    • Impact: Distorts high-frequency formants and MFCCs.
    • Mitigation: Soft-margin energy VAD stripping room silence, pre-emphasis filtering (0.97), and amplitude z-normalization.
  • Risk 2: Lighting Shifts & Dynamic Head Pose Variations
    • Impact: Degrades facial bounding box detection.
    • Mitigation: Multi-backbone spatial invariance and automatic fallback to vocal prosody when visual confidence drops.
  • Risk 3: Inference Latency Bottleneck
    • Impact: Slow conversational turnaround reduces user rapport.
    • Mitigation: Verified end-to-end latency of ~16 ms on RTX 5090 (RTF << 1.0), leaving ample headroom for dialog generation.
Supervisor Alignment: Progress is synchronized with weekly attendance sheets and verified by Dr. Ijaz Hussain and Dr. Noman Mazhar.
